To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inelastic electron-scattered cross section of H and He in the region of the delta resonance is similar to the free-nucleon result.
the delta region is suppressed by about 50% in nuclei compared to the free nucleon case.
the inelastic electron scattering of H, He and C at 730 MeV and 37.1 degrees is dominated by the delta resonance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inelastic scattering of electrons by nuclei.
the study of electron scattering from the nucleons in nuclei.
the study of the nuclear effects in the excitation region of the delta resonance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the delta region of the nuclear response is similar in all nuclei, and that the nuclear response is enhanced over that of the free proton by about a factor of three.
, although the delta resonance region is not a region of simple delta excitation, the data do show that the delta resonance region can be used to study the properties of the delta resonance.
the nuclear response in the excitation region of the delta is quite similar to the nucleon response for all nuclei from A = 1 to A = 16.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nuclear response in the 230-550 MeV region of the excitation spectrum can be explained by the nuclear medium modification of the delta resonance.
